description: AstroNvim is an aesthetic and feature-rich neovim config that is extensible and easy to use with a great set of plugins
summary: AstroNvim is a preconfigured Neovim distribution written in Lua that bundles a curated set of plugins for LSP, completion, Treesitter, file browsing, fuzzy finding, debugging, and git into a ready-to-use setup. It is aimed at developers who want a full IDE-like editor in the terminal without assembling and tuning their own Neovim config from scratch, and it can be extended through its community plugin collection.

description: Explain complex systems using visuals and simple terms. Help you prepare for system design interviews.
summary: A free educational repository of visual explanations of system design concepts, covering topics like load balancers, caching, databases, message queues, and API design, with links to longer guides. It is used by software engineers and students preparing for system design interviews and by developers who want a visual overview of how large-scale systems work.

description: Open-source, local-first apps.
summary: Epicenter is a TypeScript monorepo framework for building local-first apps whose data lives in a Yjs CRDT document on the user's machine and syncs across devices when signed in. It is aimed at developers who want offline-capable Svelte and Tauri desktop apps with self-hostable sync, and it ships a Honeycrisp markdown notes app as its first example. It is licensed AGPL-3.0-or-later.

description: Neovim config for the lazy
summary: LazyVim is a Neovim configuration framework built on lazy.nvim that turns Neovim into a full IDE with sane defaults, pre-configured plugins, and easy customization. It is used by developers who want a ready-made Neovim setup that they can still tweak, sitting between a distro and a blank config.

description: Faster Whisper transcription with CTranslate2
summary: faster-whisper is a Python library that reimplements OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model on the CTranslate2 inference engine, transcribing audio to timestamped text faster and with less memory than the original. Developers use it to add speech-to-text, subtitle generation, and word-level timestamps to their own applications, and it also backs several community tools such as speech servers and transcription GUIs.

description: Actix Web is a powerful, pragmatic, and extremely fast web framework for Rust.
summary: Actix Web is a Rust web framework for building HTTP servers, APIs, and WebSocket services on top of the Actix actor runtime and async I/O. Rust developers use it to build high-throughput back ends that need type-safe routing, middleware, and request extractors.

description: A cross-platform, OpenGL terminal emulator.
summary: Alacritty is a cross-platform, GPU-accelerated terminal emulator written in Rust that renders text with OpenGL and aims for high throughput with sensible defaults. It is used by developers and power users on Linux, macOS, Windows, and BSD who want a fast terminal configured through a TOML file, and it is considered beta-quality but used as a daily driver by many.

description: A list of Free Software network services and web applications which can be hosted on your own servers
summary: A curated, community-maintained list of free software network services and web applications that can be self-hosted on your own servers, organized by category such as analytics, email, file transfer, and password management. It helps people find alternatives to SaaS products they would rather run themselves, and is used by self-hosting enthusiasts, sysadmins, and privacy-minded developers looking for software to deploy.

description: A free, open source, and extensible speech-to-text application that works completely offline.
summary: Handy is a free, open source desktop speech-to-text app for Windows, macOS, and Linux that transcribes speech locally using Whisper or Parakeet models. You press a shortcut, speak, and the text is pasted into whatever text field is active, with no audio sent to the cloud. It is aimed at people who want private, offline dictation and accessibility tooling without a paywall.

description: An open-source, self-hostable PaaS alternative to Vercel, Heroku & Netlify that lets you easily deploy static sites, databases, full-stack applications and 360+ one-click services on your own servers.
summary: Coolify is a self-hostable deployment platform that works as an open-source alternative to Heroku, Netlify, and Vercel. It lets you deploy apps, static sites, and databases, plus hundreds of one-click services, onto your own VPS or bare-metal servers over SSH. Developers and small teams use it to keep control of their infrastructure without paying for a managed PaaS.

description: A modern runtime for JavaScript and TypeScript.
summary: Deno is a JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly runtime built on V8, Rust, and Tokio, with secure defaults that require explicit permissions for network and file access. It serves developers who want to run scripts, build web servers, and write server-side or command-line programs without a separate build toolchain or package manager setup.

description: Get your documents ready for gen AI
summary: Docling is a Python document conversion library that parses PDFs, Office files, HTML, audio and more into a unified structured format, exporting to Markdown, HTML or JSON. It is used by developers building retrieval and RAG pipelines, who need clean text and tables from documents for LLM and generative AI workflows, and it can run locally for sensitive or air-gapped data.

description: Learn how to design large-scale systems. Prep for the system design interview.  Includes Anki flashcards.
summary: The System Design Primer is an open source, self-study collection of notes, diagrams, sample solutions, and Anki flashcard decks for learning how to design large-scale distributed systems. It covers topics such as load balancing, caching, database sharding, CAP theorem, and message queues, and it works as interview prep for software engineers at companies that include system design rounds.

description: egui: an easy-to-use immediate mode GUI in Rust that runs on both web and native
summary: egui is an immediate mode GUI library written in pure Rust that runs on the web via WebAssembly and natively on desktop. It lets developers build simple interactive interfaces without callbacks, and it can be embedded in game engines or used through its eframe framework for standalone apps. Rust developers building tools, prototypes, or in-game debug panels use it.

description: An extremely fast bundler for the web
summary: esbuild is a JavaScript and TypeScript bundler and minifier written in Go that packages web code for deployment with very fast build times. It bundles ESM and CommonJS modules, handles TypeScript, JSX, and CSS natively, and offers CLI, JavaScript, and Go APIs plus a plugin system. Frontend and web developers use it as a build tool for web apps and libraries as an alternative to slower bundlers.

description: An open-source framework for making universal native apps with React. Expo runs on Android, iOS, and the web.
summary: Expo is an open-source framework for building universal native apps with React and JavaScript that run on Android, iOS, and the web. It bundles an SDK, runtime, CLI, router, and the Expo Go app so developers can ship one codebase to multiple platforms. It is used by app developers and teams who want React Native development with hosted build and deployment services.

description: Supercharge your AI agents with data from the web and beyond. Building the library for superintelligence. 🔥
summary: Firecrawl is a web data API that searches the web, scrapes pages into clean markdown or structured JSON, crawls whole sites, and maps URLs for AI applications. It solves the problem of getting reliable, LLM-ready web content without managing proxies, JavaScript rendering, or rate limits. It is used by developers building AI agents, RAG pipelines, and data extraction tools, and it is available as open source self-hosted code or as a hosted service.

description: Port of OpenAI's Whisper model in C/C++
summary: whisper.cpp is a dependency-free C/C++ port of OpenAI's Whisper automatic speech recognition model, letting you transcribe audio files and microphone input entirely offline. It is used by developers who want fast, local speech-to-text on laptops, phones, Raspberry Pi and servers, with GPU and NPU acceleration backends.

description: Blazing 💥 fast terminal-ui for git written in rust 🦀
summary: GitUI is a terminal user interface app for working with git repositories, offering a keyboard-driven, GUI-like experience for staging, committing, diffing, stashing, branching, pushing and fetching. It is aimed at developers who want a fast alternative to git GUIs like lazygit or tig, especially on very large repositories where other tools freeze.

description: A post-modern modal text editor.
summary: Helix is a terminal-based modal text editor written in Rust, inspired by Kakoune and Neovim, with Vim-like modal editing and multiple selections. It provides built-in language server support and syntax highlighting via tree-sitter, aimed at developers who want a fast, batteries-included code editor in the terminal.

description: A cross-platform GUI library for Rust, inspired by Elm
summary: Iced is a cross-platform GUI library for Rust that lets developers build desktop and web user interfaces using a type-safe, Elm-inspired architecture of state, messages, view, and update. It is aimed at Rust developers who want to write native graphical applications for Windows, macOS, Linux, and the web, with built-in widgets, async support, and wgpu or tiny-skia renderers. The project is still experimental, so it suits developers willing to track a changing API.

description: Python tool for converting files and office documents to Markdown.
summary: MarkItDown is a Python library and command-line tool that converts PDFs, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, HTML, images, audio, EPUB, and other files into Markdown while preserving headings, lists, tables, and links. It is aimed at developers building LLM and text analysis pipelines who need document content in a token-efficient text format rather than high-fidelity human-readable output.

description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability
summary: Neovim is a text editor and terminal application that is a refactored, extensible fork of Vim, with an embeddable API, Lua scripting, and support for external GUIs. It is used by developers and system administrators who want a modern, scriptable Vim-style editor that still runs most existing Vim plugins.

description: ☁️ Nextcloud server, a safe home for all your data
summary: Nextcloud Server is a self-hosted file sync, sharing, and collaboration platform, a private alternative to Dropbox or Google Drive. It lets individuals, families, and organizations store files, calendars, and contacts on their own hardware or a chosen provider, with an extensible app ecosystem. It is used by home users, businesses, and public sector and education organizations that want control over their data.

description: Node.js JavaScript runtime ✨🐢🚀✨
summary: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime that lets developers run JavaScript outside the browser, typically on servers, command-line tools, and build pipelines. It is the reference implementation of the server-side JavaScript platform, built on the V8 engine, and is used by web developers, backend engineers, and tooling authors.

description: A launch point for your personal nvim configuration
summary: A single-file Neovim configuration template in Lua that serves as a commented starting point for building your own personal editor setup, rather than a full distribution. It is aimed at developers who want to learn Neovim and Lua by reading and extending a well-documented init.lua that uses the built-in vim.pack plugin manager.

description: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision
summary: Whisper is an open-source speech recognition model and Python library that transcribes audio to text, translates non-English speech into English, and identifies spoken languages. It is used by developers and researchers who need multilingual transcription, subtitling, or speech-to-text features in their own tools, run from the command line or Python.

description: Incredibly fast JavaScript runtime, bundler, test runner, and package manager – all in one
summary: Bun is an all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript toolkit distributed as a single executable, acting as a fast runtime, bundler, test runner, script runner, and package manager. It serves as a drop-in replacement for Node.js and npm, aimed at developers who want faster startup and fewer separate tools in their JavaScript and TypeScript projects.

description: ⚓ A collection of high-performance JavaScript tools.
summary: Oxc is a collection of high-performance JavaScript and TypeScript tools written in Rust, including a parser, transformer, minifier, module resolver, linter (Oxlint), and formatter (Oxfmt). It addresses the slowness of existing JavaScript build, lint, and format tooling on large codebases. Build tool authors and frontend developers use it, and it powers the Rolldown bundler used by Vite.

description: A Rust crate for cooking up terminal user interfaces (TUIs) 👨‍🍳🐀 https://ratatui.rs
summary: Ratatui is a Rust library crate for building text-based terminal user interfaces (TUIs) with widgets, layouts, and rendering. Rust developers use it to create command-line applications, dashboards, and interactive console programs, and it is a maintained fork of the tui-rs crate.

description: A curated list of Rust code and resources.
summary: A community-maintained, curated list of Rust crates, applications, tools, and learning resources organized by category. Developers use it as a discovery index to find libraries and projects for a specific need, such as web frameworks, embedded work, or async runtimes.

description: 💬📝 A small dictation app using OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition model.
summary: WhisperWriter is a small Python speech-to-text dictation app that records from a microphone on a keyboard shortcut and types the transcription into the active window. It transcribes locally with faster-whisper or through the OpenAI Whisper API, and it offers several recording modes such as continuous, press-to-toggle, and hold-to-record. It is aimed at people who want hands-free typing on their desktop.

description: Build smaller, faster, and more secure desktop and mobile applications with a web frontend.
summary: Tauri is a Rust framework for building small, fast desktop and mobile applications that use a web frontend such as React, Vue, or Svelte for the user interface. It wraps the system webview with a Rust backend, so developers can ship native apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android without bundling a full browser like Electron does. It is aimed at developers who already build web interfaces and want lightweight native binaries with a secure Rust-side API.

description: HTTP routing and request-handling library for Rust that focuses on ergonomics and modularity
summary: Axum is a web application framework library for Rust that provides HTTP routing and request handling built on top of the Tokio async runtime and the Tower middleware ecosystem. It lets developers define typed extractors, handlers, and modular routers to build HTTP APIs and web services. It is used by Rust backend developers who want an ergonomic, composable alternative to heavier web frameworks.

description: Open-source web crawler and scraper for LLMs and AI agents: any website into clean, LLM-ready Markdown. Run it yourself, or use Crawl4AI Cloud with one key. Join our Discord https://discord.gg/VuxzM8mtf
summary: Crawl4AI is an open-source Python web crawler and scraper that converts any website into clean, LLM-ready Markdown and structured JSON for RAG pipelines and AI agents. Developers run it themselves as a library, CLI, or Docker server, or use the hosted Crawl4AI Cloud API with an MCP endpoint for agents.

description: Next generation frontend tooling. It's fast!
summary: Vite is a frontend build tool that pairs a fast dev server, using native ES modules and instant hot module replacement, with a production bundler powered by Rolldown. Web developers use it to scaffold, develop, and bundle modern JavaScript and TypeScript projects, and it has a plugin API for extending the build.

description: A terminal workspace with batteries included
summary: Zellij is a terminal workspace and multiplexer written in Rust that lets you split a terminal into multiple panes, tabs, and floating or stacked windows. It adds layouts for scripted session setups, a plugin system using WebAssembly, real-time multi-user collaboration, and a built-in web client. It is aimed at developers and ops engineers who work in the terminal and want an alternative to tmux or GNU Screen.

description: 🤗 Transformers: the model-definition framework for state-of-the-art machine learning models in text, vision, audio, and multimodal models, for both inference and training.
summary: Hugging Face Transformers is a Python library of pretrained model definitions for text, vision, audio, video, and multimodal machine learning, covering both inference and training with PyTorch. It lets developers load and run or fine-tune thousands of models from the Hugging Face Hub through a unified API, such as the pipeline interface for generation, classification, and speech recognition. It is used by ML researchers, engineers, and developers, and its model definitions are supported by many training frameworks and inference engines.

description: A list of SaaS, PaaS and IaaS offerings that have free tiers of interest to devops and infradev
summary: free-for.dev is an curated awesome list of software-as-a-service, platform-as-a-service, and infrastructure-as-a-service offerings that have free developer tiers, filtered for DevOps and infrastructure engineers. It helps system administrators and DevOps practitioners find cloud, CI/CD, monitoring, and hosting services they can use without paying, organized by category with free-tier limits noted. The list is maintained by volunteers through pull requests and only includes hosted services, not self-hosted software.

description: :electron: Build cross-platform desktop apps with JavaScript, HTML, and CSS
summary: Electron is a cross-platform desktop application framework that lets developers build native-feeling apps for macOS, Windows, and Linux using JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. It combines Node.js with the Chromium rendering engine so web developers can ship desktop software without learning platform-specific toolkits. It is used by teams building editors, chat clients, and other desktop tools, including Visual Studio Code.

description: VoiceStudio is the open-source, fully-local ElevenLabs alternative — voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription & audiobook creation in 646 languages.
summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source, local-first AI voice studio that runs on desktop, mobile and server hardware. It handles voice cloning, voice design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription and audiobook narration across 646 languages, with no paid cloud required. It is aimed at creators, localizers and developers who want an ElevenLabs-style text-to-speech tool that keeps their audio on their own device.

description: web development for the rest of us
summary: Svelte is a JavaScript compiler and UI framework for building web applications. It converts declarative components into efficient vanilla JavaScript that updates the DOM directly, avoiding a runtime virtual DOM. Web developers use it as an alternative to React, Vue, and Angular for building single-page apps and websites.

description: Transforms complex documents like PDFs and Office docs into LLM-ready markdown/JSON for your Agentic workflows.
summary: MinerU is an open-source document parser that converts PDFs, scanned images, and Office files such as DOCX, PPTX, and XLSX into Markdown or JSON suitable for LLM pipelines and retrieval-augmented generation. It also offers a command-line tool, Python SDK, and API for document library search and page-by-page reading. Developers building AI agents, RAG systems, and data extraction workflows use it as an alternative to generic PDF parsers and OCR libraries.

description: The Patterns of Scalable, Reliable, and Performant Large-Scale Systems
summary: A curated GitHub reading list of articles, engineering blog posts, talks, and books on designing scalable, reliable, and performant large-scale distributed systems. It organizes case studies from companies like Netflix, Uber, and Twitter by topics such as caching, microservices, distributed locking, tracing, and scheduling. Software engineers and architects use it to study system design patterns and prepare for system design interviews.

description: A bundler for javascript and friends. Packs many modules into a few bundled assets. Code Splitting allows for loading parts of the application on demand. Through "loaders", modules can be CommonJs, AMD, ES6 modules, CSS, Images, JSON, Coffeescript, LESS, ... and your custom stuff.
summary: Webpack is a JavaScript module bundler that packs many modules and assets into a few output files, with code splitting to load parts of an app on demand. Loaders let it process CommonJS, AMD, ES modules, CSS, images, JSON, and other file types, and a plugin system extends it further. Web developers and frontend teams use it as a build tool for bundling browser applications.

description: 后端架构师技术图谱
summary: A Chinese-language backend architecture knowledge map, organized as an awesome-style list of links covering data structures, algorithms, concurrency, operating systems, design patterns, middleware, databases, networking, security, and distributed systems. Backend developers and architects in Chinese-speaking communities use it as a study guide and reference index for interview preparation and technical self-learning.

description: :atom: The hackable text editor
summary: Atom is a free, open-source, hackable text editor built on Electron for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It lets developers write and edit code and prose with a highly customizable interface and a large ecosystem of community packages. Its maintainers announced in 2022 that the project would be archived in December 2022, so it is no longer actively developed.

description: The open-source AI voice studio. Clone, dictate, create.
summary: Voicebox is a local-first, open-source voice studio that clones voices from a few seconds of audio, generates speech across multiple TTS engines, and provides global dictation with Whisper transcription. It runs entirely on the user's machine as a desktop app (Tauri) with a REST API and MCP server, so developers and creators can use it as a free, private alternative to cloud services like ElevenLabs and WisprFlow.

description: Open-Source Frontier Voice AI
summary: VibeVoice is Microsoft's open-source family of voice AI models, covering long-form speech recognition (ASR) that transcribes up to 60 minutes of audio with speaker labels and timestamps, multi-speaker text-to-speech for podcast-style audio up to 90 minutes, and a lightweight real-time streaming TTS model. It is aimed at researchers and developers building speech transcription or speech synthesis pipelines, and the README states the models are intended for research and development rather than commercial use without further testing.

description: Learn how to design systems at scale and prepare for system design interviews
summary: A free, open-source system design course covering networking, databases, distributed systems, and architecture patterns, with worked examples of designing large-scale services. It is aimed at software engineers preparing for system design interviews and at developers who want to learn how to design systems that scale.
